newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan government's assessment of economy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Japan government's assessment of economy unchanged.

text.p: The Japanese government kept its assessment of the economy unchanged on Tuesday, saying it was continuing on a path of gradual recovery.
The phraseology of the Economic Planning Agency's (EPA) monthly economic report, which is closely watched by markets for signs of policy shift, was unchanged from November.
"Our country's economy continues to recover, although the pace of the recovery is slow," the December report said.

But as a sign of the government's increasing optimism, the report noted that industrial production was increasing, moving a step forward from the previous month, when the EPA said output was "gradually" increasing.

The high pace of automobile production was the main element supporting output growth, an EPA official told reporters, adding that a steady rise in output of communications-related products had also contributed to the overall growth.

The official said a fall in semiconductor production was bottoming out, but the outlook for a recovery of that sector was still uncertain. He also said that some industries, such as those producing basic materials, had a tendency to overproduce, which affected inventory adjustment. But "overall, production is on an increase," he said.
The report also said exports remained strong, due to increased exports of electrical equipment to Asian nations and of car parts.

Asked what it would take for the government to move its assessment of the economy a step further, the EPA official said: "The key is whether private demand will continue to show a steady rise at a time when public demand is shrinking."

The official said capital investment had picked up, particularly in the latter half of the current fiscal year, and housing starts had risen at an unusually high pace due to demand before the planned sales tax increase next April.
Industrial production was also showing signs of steady increase, and "the key is whether these (signs of increasing private demand) will continue in the future," he said.
The EPA has for most of this year described Japan's economy as gradually recovering, despite some weakness after years of negligible growth.
November's report retained the familiar reference to gradual economic recovery, but moved an inch forward by deleting the phrase "there are some worrying aspects" from its overall assessment.

December's report said bank lending had dropped from the previous year and government bond yields remained low. This reflected uncertainty in financial markets about the future of Japan's economy, despite signs of brightness in the real economy, the official said.

"There is a consensus that the economic recovery is increasing its steadiness, but I believe the low yields in government bonds reflect the fact that neither the financial markets nor the economists have a clear picture of the future (of Japan's economy)," he said.
